claims.author: jeanpablojp
claims.harm: test flakiness and false failures when a second rollover occurs between setting now and client idle stamping
claims.quote: now is a whole second, taken before the clients exist and compared against an m_idle_since they stamp later, so the checks expecting a disconnect at now + timeout + 1s only hold while both fall in the same second.

settled_by.quote: Opted for mocking the clock and freeze it rather than trying to keep up with the current time of the actual clock as it drifts throughout the added test case.

claims.author: jeanpablojp
claims.harm: accepted connections that send nothing prevent fast shutdown or exhaust RPC slots when -rpcservertimeout=0
claims.quote: A connection that is accepted and never sends anything keeps m_connection_busy at its initial true, so the disconnect_all branch never picks it up. Inside ShouldDisconnect() only the idle timeout is left, and with -rpcservertimeout=0 there is no idle timeout either.

settled_by.quote: Agreed it does not belong here though, and your five seconds sounds like the right direction. Happy to open a follow-up.

notes: jeanpablojp raised concerns about clock rollover in unit tests (resolved by mocking the clock) and delayed shutdown on idle connections (resolved as pre-existing behavior deferred to a follow-up). winterrdog provided a Tested ACK. / Initial record. Recorded two resolved claims from jeanpablojp regarding unit test timing sensitivity (fixed by mocking the clock) and pre-existing idle client shutdown behavior (agreed out of scope for a follow-up).
